idiom_name: spdlog custom sink (spdlog::sinks::base_sink<Mutex>) with chained HMAC
implementation_notes: spdlog supplies the chokepoint: derive from spdlog::sinks::base_sink<Mutex> (or <spdlog::details::null_mutex> only under a single writer) and chain a MAC over the formatted payload, the sequence number and the previous tag, keeping the chain state in the sink. The classic hand-written form stays justified when spdlog must not enter the dependency set, when records need an asymmetric signature, or when the sink has to own its O_APPEND/fsync policy - the OpenSSL variant below covers exactly that case, and both variants share the same verifier contract.
pitfalls: base_sink serialises sink_it_ across threads through its mutex template argument; using base_sink<null_mutex> without an external single writer makes the chain state race.
The chain state must be restored (or the head anchored) on rotation and restart - a fresh prev_ silently starts a new half-chain that verifies against nothing.
spdlog formats the message before the sink sees it, so redaction and canonicalisation must happen in the pattern formatter or before the log call; the sink cannot redact what it never saw.

variants.name: Application-owned appender over OpenSSL EVP_MAC
variants.idiom_name: EVP_MAC HMAC/SHA-256 chain in an application-owned appender class
variants.implementation_notes: No logging dependency: the sink is your own appender class that keeps the previous tag and a monotonic sequence number and computes the chained tag with the OpenSSL 3 EVP_MAC API (HMAC with SHA-256; the older HMAC_* context functions are deprecated). Choose this variant when the audit log must be verifiable against a published head tag, when records are signed rather than MACed, or when spdlog cannot be added; you now own rotation, fsync policy and thread-safety yourself.
pitfalls: OpenSSL 3.0 deprecated HMAC_CTX_* in favour of EVP_MAC_*; code written against the old context API is on a removal path and hidden by OPENSSL_API_COMPAT.
The EVP_MAC_CTX is not thread-safe: one context per writer, and free it with EVP_MAC_CTX_free (it holds key material in memory).
